evidence.summary: Points (0,0),(0,1) can split across halves and be counted although strict x fails.
Subtraction is not associative: (a-b)-c differs from a-(b-c), so combining independently folded prefix and suffix is not generally the original ordered fold.
Each retained point-update version path-copies up to D+1 nodes; sharing untouched subtrees gives O(qD), not O(q) when D varies.
Bellman-Ford handles negative edges without reachable negative cycles and O(VE) fits the stated limits; a standard-route replacement is unnecessary.
n=0 calls solve(0,-1); l==r is false and recursion does not have a valid decreasing interval base.
Insert 7, delete 7, insert 7 yields true,false,true, so a false midpoint cannot discard the entire earlier half.
Equal x violates strictness across a split; C(200000,2)=19999900000 exceeds signed 32-bit.
Sending flow on a positive-cost forward edge creates a residual reverse edge with the negated, hence negative, cost; unweighted Dijkstra premises fail.
The prompt records a real seed, budget, and small domain, which supports only no mismatch in that range.
Add then cover and cover then add require different composed tags; patch only pushdown() to preserve chronological composition.
The recorded base seed, case seed, iteration and differing fifth output make the random run reproducible.

After an older add and a newer assignment coexist, descending propagates the stale add after the set; assignment must clear the previous pending addition. Any minimized case must pass a legality validator and reproduce both outputs.

conditions: For half-open intervals [l,r), equality next.left=last.right is non-overlapping and the rule is valid.
For closed intervals [l,r], touching at an endpoint overlaps, so acceptance requires next.left>last.right.
